items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You were talking about Joe Gloriosa when the machine was off.

ctx.x: Jazz festival open Thursday. Jazz concerts and... I don't know who this is. That must be... Larry Wilson. Larry Wilson yeah. From WNO. You see this see this job right here? Monk was so drunk on this truck that when he went to get off of there he fell off on the ground. On the street and nearly killed him. What were we all doing? Well we were playing on the street but Monk come on a job. Came on a job drunk. We were balli-hooing a concert at the auditorium that Sunday afternoon.

So you can get used to watching the machine. See if it's picking up. Testing. Yeah. You and Jim have voices that broadcast. Yeah well we got a bow bow on something. Which one? You were talking about Joe Gloriosa when the machine was off. Mmhmm. See the Flamingo Lounge 405 bourbon. Yeah. Bert Adam owned that. Bert Adam. It was Adam. A-D-A-M. They got B-E-R-T. A-D-A-M-S and it's and it was no S. No.

Who was Cecilia Kirsch? Cecilia Kirsch was a fine little singer and she was in love with a boy named Jock Robinson. Jock was playing with a very fine little band over on the Gulf Coast and she married Jock and they had I think four children. When Jock was on his way to St. Thomas Catholic Church in Long Beach when a drunk came along in a speeding automobile and hit him head on, hit his car head on and killed Jock.
